name: uk-home-education-reports
description: Helps UK home-educating parents turn rough learning notes into clear, structured home education reports.

interface.longDescription: Turn rough notes about a child's home education into a clear, structured UK home education report. Designed for home-educating parents who want help organising activities, interests, learning examples, observations and progress without inventing evidence or forcing a school-style format. Supports England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. Not legal advice.
defaultPrompt: Turn my notes into a home education report.
Help me structure a UK home education report.
Create a report from the learning activities I've described.

positive.description: Create a report from several months of home education activities and observations.
positive.prompt: I home educate my 10-year-old in England. Over the last six months we've done lots of baking, library trips, gardening and nature walks. She's been reading independently more often, weighing ingredients herself and became really interested in identifying birds. Can you turn this into a home education report?
positive.expected_behavior: Create a structured England home education report using only the supplied activities and observations. The report may identify learning that is genuinely evidenced by the notes, but must not invent progress, achievements, activities or unsupported learning outcomes.

positive.description: Create a Wales home education report suitable in tone for a local authority update.
positive.prompt: I'm in Wales and need to send our local authority an update about my 12-year-old. He's mostly child-led. Recently he's been interested in penguins, went to the zoo, read the information signs, watched documentaries about Antarctica and looked up different penguin species at home. Please make this into a report.
positive.expected_behavior: Create a structured Wales home education report from the supplied evidence, preserving the child-led approach and avoiding unsupported legal claims or invented progress.

positive.description: Turn rough mixed home education notes into a structured report.
positive.prompt: These are my messy home ed notes from this year in Scotland: woodworking with grandad, measured timber for a bird box, worked out where to put it, lots of fantasy reading, some multiplication and money work, bike rides and weekly swimming. Can you organise this properly into a home education report?
positive.expected_behavior: Convert the rough notes into a clear structured Scotland home education report without requiring the parent to rewrite them first. Preserve practical and interest-led learning and do not force every activity into school-style subject categories.

positive.description: Improve a brief existing home education report draft without adding unsupported detail.
positive.prompt: I'm home educating in England. Between January and September 2026 Sam has read lots, cooked with me, used money in shops, built things in Minecraft and visited a science museum. Can you turn that into a better home education report without making anything up?
positive.expected_behavior: Produce a clearer and more useful home education report from the supplied draft while staying strictly within the facts provided. Do not invent reading materials, skills, progress, achievements, museum exhibits or educational outcomes.

positive.description: Create a proportionately short report when the parent has only sparse but usable information.
positive.prompt: We're in Northern Ireland. My 8-year-old has mainly been building dens, riding his bike, listening to audiobooks and making things from cardboard this summer. We haven't done formal lessons. That's honestly most of what I have written down. Please make the report anyway.
positive.expected_behavior: Generate a concise Northern Ireland home education report based only on the supplied activities. Do not pad the report, invent progress or repeatedly frame the education negatively because formal lessons were not used. A factual warning about sparse information may be returned if appropriate.

negative.description: Do not use the home education report tool for ordinary school reports.
negative.prompt: I'm a primary school teacher. Can you write end-of-year school reports for my class?

negative.description: Do not use the report tool for lesson planning.
negative.prompt: Can you make me a five-day Year 6 maths lesson plan covering fractions and percentages?

negative.description: Do not call the report tool before any usable home education information has been supplied.
negative.prompt: Make me a home education report.

publication.release_notes: Initial release of UK Home Education Reports by Strew. Adds a UK-focused home education report workflow using the create_home_education_report MCP tool, with support for England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. Reports are generated from user-supplied learning notes and are designed not to invent activities, progress, achievements or evidence.
